relevance_reason: The abstract reports two CFAP47 variants in one man with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF), with reduced CFAP47 and WDR87 in his sperm. It also shows that WDR87 interacts with CFAP47, which supports CFAP47-related spermatogenic failure (SPGFX3).

findings.statement: Liao et al. (2022) screened 7 men with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF) for gene mutations. In one of them they found two novel variants in the CFAP47 gene: c.706G>A (Val236Met) and c.1337C>T (Thr446Met).
quotes: Subsequently, we screened gene mutations in seven MMAF individuals and found two novel mutations in CFAP47 (c.706G>A, Val236Met; c.1337C>T, Thr446Met) in one case.

phenotypes.text: multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella

findings.statement: Liao et al. (2022) found by immunoblotting and immunofluorescence that CFAP47 was dramatically reduced in sperm from the man with the CFAP47 variants. WDR87 expression was also significantly reduced, with weak signals next to the sperm nuclei. The authors concluded that CFAP47 was needed to transport WDR87 during the formation of the sperm flagellum.
quotes: Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence revealed that CFAP47 was dramatically reduced in spermatozoa from the CFAP47-mutated man.

Meanwhile, the expression of WDR87 was also significantly decreased, and weak signals were detected adjacent to the spermatozoa nuclei, indicating that CFAP47 was necessary for WDR87 transportation during spermatozoa flagella biogenesis.

findings.statement: Liao et al. (2022) found that WDR87 was highly expressed in human and mouse testis. In mice it sat in the cytoplasm around the nucleus of spermatocytes and round spermatids, moved to the manchette during spermiogenesis, and ended up in the middle piece of the sperm tail. They identified CFAP47 as a protein that interacts with WDR87 in the sperm flagellar midpiece. They concluded that the two proteins form a complex involved in assembling the sperm tail.
quotes: In the spermiogenesis stage, with extension of the nucleus, WDR87 migrated to the manchette and finally localized to the middle piece of the spermatozoa tail.

Furthermore, we identified a cilia- and flagella-associated protein, CFAP47, which interacted with WDR87 in the flagellar midpiece of the spermatozoa, suggesting that WDR87 may be associated with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF).
These data indicate that WDR87 is located in the middle piece of the sperm tail and interacts with CFAP47 to form a complex which is involved in spermatozoa tail assembly.

relevance_reason: Identifies hemizygous CFAP47 variants as the cause of X-linked MMAF/asthenoteratozoospermia (SPGFX3), and includes a mouse model.

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2021) reported 3 unrelated Chinese men with primary infertility caused by asthenoteratozoospermia characterized by multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF), as well as an Australian man with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. The authors stated that all men carrying hemizygous CFAP47 variants had typical MMAF phenotypes.
quotes: identified hemizygous missense variants in the X-linked CFAP47 in three unrelated Chinese individuals with MMAF
All men harboring hemizygous CFAP47 variants displayed typical MMAF phenotypes.

phenotypes.text: multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella

findings.statement: In 3 unrelated Chinese men with MMAF, Liu et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to identify hemizygous missense variants in the X-linked CFAP47 gene. The 3 variants were absent from human control population genome databases and were predicted to be deleterious by multiple bioinformatic tools. Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed obviously reduced CFAP47 levels in spermatozoa from all 3 men.
quotes: identified hemizygous missense variants in the X-linked CFAP47 in three unrelated Chinese individuals with MMAF
These three CFAP47 variants were absent in human control population genome databases and were predicted to be deleterious by multiple bioinformatic tools.
Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence assays revealed obviously reduced levels of CFAP47 in spermatozoa from all three men harboring deleterious missense variants of CFAP47.

findings.statement: Using whole-exome sequencing data from an additional cohort of men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia from Australia, Liu et al. (2021) identified a hemizygous deletion at Xp21.1 that removed the entire CFAP47 gene.
quotes: WES data from an additional cohort of severe asthenoteratozoospermic men originating from Australia permitted the identification of a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene.

variants.as_reported: hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2021) noted that CFAP47 encodes a cilia- and flagella-associated protein that is highly expressed in testis.
quotes: CFAP47 encodes a cilia- and flagella-associated protein that is highly expressed in testis.

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2021) generated a Cfap47-mutated mouse model. Adult male mutant mice were sterile and had reduced sperm motility and abnormal flagellar morphology and movement, but fertility could be rescued by intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI).
quotes: We also generated a Cfap47-mutated mouse model, the adult males of which were sterile and presented with reduced sperm motility and abnormal flagellar morphology and movement.
However, fertility could be rescued by the use of intra-cytoplasmic sperm injections (ICSIs).

findings.statement: Based on findings in humans and mice, Liu et al. (2021) concluded that hemizygous CFAP47 mutations cause X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia, and suggested a good prognosis with ICSI.
quotes: hemizygous mutations in CFAP47 can induce X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia, for which good ICSI prognosis is suggested.
